orig_text:
When destroying push subscriptions that include the data type PushSubscription, 
the server MAY issue one final StateChange push notification using the old URL and 
application server key to notify the client of changes to the PushSubscription data type. 
This prompts the client to make a PushSubscription/changes method call. The response 
to this call will contain an updated sessionState, which refers to a session object that 
contains the new VAPID key.
notes:
The PushSubscription object is not associated with an account id, and so cannot appear in 
the StateChange object as specified in RFC8620. Additionally, there is no 
"PushSubscription/changes" method call defined in RFC8620 — only "PushSubscription/get" 
and "PushSubscription/set".

Suggested fix is to remove this paragraph. There is no good way of doing this right now, 
and it was a MAY anyway, not essential. Session state changes are likely to be picked up 
very quickly by a client anyway as they will get it as soon as they make any API call.
